title: Security in LLM-Assisted Coding: A Systematic Literature Review
abstract: arXiv:2610.15482v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Large Language Models accelerate software development but introduce severe security vulnerabilities. This systematic review investigates security risks in automated coding, benchmark limitations, and the role of human developers. Findings indicate that models frequently generate insecure code and faulty patches due to training data biases. Additionally, the models themselves are susceptible to direct attacks. Current evaluation methods suffer from data contamination and lack robust security metrics. Consequently, human oversight remains essential. Safer integration of automation will require more security-aware model architectures, stronger security-specific benchmarks, and more effective human-AI collaboration frameworks to mitigate these systemic risks.

translated_title: 大语言模型辅助编程中的安全性：系统性文献综述
translated_abstract: 大语言模型加速了软件开发，但同时也带来了严重的安全漏洞。本系统性综述研究了自动化编码中的安全风险、基准测试的局限性以及人类开发者的作用。研究结果表明，由于训练数据的偏差，模型经常生成不安全的代码和有缺陷的补丁。此外，模型本身也容易受到直接攻击。当前的评估方法存在数据污染问题，且缺乏健壮的安全度量指标。因此，人类监督仍然不可或缺。要更安全地集成自动化技术，将需要更具安全意识的模型架构、更强大的安全专用基准测试，以及更有效的人机协作框架，以缓解这些系统性风险。
tldr: 本系统性综述揭示了LLM辅助编程因训练数据偏差而频繁生成不安全代码和错误补丁、模型自身易受攻击、现有基准存在数据污染等系统性风险，并指出需要安全感知的模型架构、安全专用基准测试与有效的人机协作框架来保障安全。
en_tdlr: This systematic literature review reveals that LLM-assisted coding frequently produces insecure code and faulty patches due to training data biases, models themselves are vulnerable to direct attacks, and current benchmarks suffer from data contamination, calling for security-aware model architectures, robust security-specific benchmarks, and effective human-AI collaboration frameworks.
